ETH.data_source: 1000BASE-T1 (IEEE 802.3bp); longest frame 1522 B tagged + 8 B preamble + 12 B gap
ETH.hop_source: store-and-forward of one longest frame at 1 Gbit/s (12.3 us) plus 2 us switch forwarding (Rox, Ernst, Giusto, DATE 2012)
ETH.cost_source: per metre: estimate: shielded automotive Ethernet pair about 3x a CAN pair (no bulk price found); per port: PHY 1000BASE-T1 TI DP83TG720 USD 11.71 at 250 pcs (Mouser) + half a sealed connector pair (USD 8-20 per pair, supplier figures; low confidence)
ETH.port_cost_note: 2026-10-29, user decision: Ethernet port cost 17.0 USD / 4 = 4.25 USD, so that a switch (SJA1110, 22.87 USD) pays off only from about 6 Ethernet ports on one ECU, instead of from 2 ports (every ECU of the 300 design had a switch at 3-9 ports)
ETH.max_length_source: 1000BASE-T1 / 100BASE-T1 link segment up to 15 m (IEEE 802.3bp / bw, automotive)

FLEXRAY.data_source: FlexRay 10 Mbit/s (ISO 17458); longest frame 262 B (254 B payload), 10 bit per byte
FLEXRAY.hop_source: a static-segment message waits up to one bus cycle for its slot; cycle 5 ms assumed (design parameter, at most 16 ms by the FlexRay specification; Pop et al., Real-Time Systems 2008)
FLEXRAY.cost_source: per metre: FLRY-A 2x0.35 mm2 twisted pair EUR 24.94 per 100 m incl. VAT (Bedia-Kabel, 500 m ring), x2 for harness making (materials are 40-65 % of a harness cost, supplier figures; low confidence); per port: transceiver NXP TJA1082 USD 3.1-4.1 + half a sealed connector pair (USD 8-20 per pair, supplier figures; low confidence)
FLEXRAY.weight_source: two FLRY 0.35 mm2 cores, 2 x 4.3 g/m (derived)
FLEXRAY.max_length_source: FlexRay electrical physical layer: up to 24 m between two nodes

CAN.data_source: high-speed CAN at 500 kbit/s (ISO 11898-2); 8-byte frame 135 bit worst case (Davis et al. 2007)
CAN.cost_source: per metre: FLRY-A 2x0.35 mm2 twisted pair EUR 24.94 per 100 m incl. VAT (Bedia-Kabel, 500 m ring), x2 for harness making (materials are 40-65 % of a harness cost, supplier figures; low confidence); per port: transceiver NXP TJA1042 USD 0.87-1.04 (1k) + half a sealed connector pair (USD 8-20 per pair, supplier figures; low confidence)
CAN.weight_source: two FLRY 0.35 mm2 cores, 2 x 4.3 g/m (derived)
CAN.max_length_source: ISO 11898-2: 40 m bus length at 1 Mbit/s

LIN.data_source: LIN at 19.2 kbit/s (ISO 17987); 8-byte frame 174 bit maximum
LIN.cost_source: per metre: FLRY-B 0.35 mm2 single core USD 0.21-0.29/m (TME, 100-500 m reels), x2 for harness making (materials are 40-65 % of a harness cost, supplier figures; low confidence); per port: transceiver NXP TJA1021 USD 0.73-0.97 (1k) + half a sealed connector pair (USD 8-20 per pair, supplier figures; low confidence)
LIN.max_length_source: LIN specification: bus length up to 40 m

UART.data_source: UART at 115.2 kbaud (typical GNSS receiver port); one 10-bit character
UART.cost_source: per metre: estimate (as a CAN pair); per port: estimate (as a LIN port)
UART.max_length_source: 115.2 kbit/s: the EIA-232 capacitance limit (2,500 pF, 50-100 pF/m cable) gives metres at this rate; 5 m assumed (low confidence)

SPI.data_source: SPI at up to 9 Mbit/s (Honeywell HG1120 IMU brochure: SPI 2-9 Mbit, RS-422/CAN 1 Mbit); one 32-bit transfer
SPI.cost_source: per metre: estimate (as a CAN pair); per port: estimate (as a LIN port)
SPI.max_length_source: board-level clocked bus: tens of cm at MHz clocks; 1 m is the upper end with buffered lines at a reduced clock (low confidence); the suite's SPI devices (IMU, brake actuators) sit 0.4-1.0 m from their nearest cell on the channel graph

backbone._comment: Candidate backbone paths per site pair handed to the optimiser: the direct link plus the (candidate_paths - 1) shortest routes over one relaying site (needs a SWITCH there); all traffic of a site pair uses one path per cable type. The traffic constraints (a pair with traffic needs a selected path, link load within cables x capacity, chain latency, failure scenarios) are lazy constraints added in a callback. path_link_cut (on): static LP strengthening, a selected path has a cable on each of its links.
backbone._bus_lines_comment: Bus lines available per bus type (CAN, LIN, FlexRay): the optimiser decides which units and devices share a line; a line is a cable through all its members (exact Steiner tree on the cable channels), its members share its bit rate. Upper limit, set by hand for now (2026-10-21): more interchangeable lines made the search much slower without a better design (lite: 4/3/2 lines 133 s, 1/2/1 lines 20 s, same optimum); a run reports when every line of a type is in use. To be replaced by an automatic bound with symmetry breaking (HANDOFF 16.12). 2026-10-22: CAN 2 and LIN 3, because with failures on a device of critical software has two lanes on two lines (steering, motor, brakes on CAN; the ASIL-3 lights on LIN, the ASIL-2 HVAC on its own LIN line).
backbone._bus_max_utilization_comment: Share of its bit rate a bus line may be loaded with (devices + unit traffic, both directions). The latency bound (every other message on a resource is sent once before a message) assumes a bus that is not saturated. Provisional 0.7 (common guidance for CAN bus load), HANDOFF 17.
backbone._priorities_comment: Fixed-priority, non-preemptive queues on every cable and bus line, as CAN arbitrates by identifier and Ethernet switches serve IEEE 802.1Q traffic classes: a chain message gets the tightest network budget of its chains (deadline-monotonic), the end device of a chain that of the chain, all other traffic comes last. A message waits for every message of equal or higher priority once and for at most one frame of a lower-priority one (cable_types.frame_kbit). false = every other message once (no priorities).
backbone._speed_options: upfront_paths / cell_cut_capacity (2026-10-24): valid extra constraints (every flow's path requirement up front; per-cell cut-set link capacity). Default off: on 10 cells they make the model 2.3x larger and no design was found within 1 h; on the lite instance (4 cells) both on proved the rho 1 failure case (8,978.26) within 1 h. Use them for proofs on small instances only. A per-failure-scenario cut-set (tag cf) was removed: invalid (a flow relayed through the failed cell is lost, not rerouted, so it carries no load; the inequality counted it and cut off the proven lite optimum). benders_cuts (2026-10-26): Benders feasibility cuts from a routing LP per candidate (benders.py); default off, measured as tag b.
backbone._bus_tree_bounds_comment: Upfront bus-line length bounds from exact Steiner trees of small member sets (2026-11-01): 'full' = device groups up to 4, each alone, with every cell and with every pair of cells (the setting of every run so far; 1.2 million rows at 500 components / 30 cells, 83 % of the model, and 870 s of tree computation per fresh process); 'one_unit' = the groups alone and with one cell; 'pairs' = only the pair and Euler-tour bounds. All variants are valid (lazy cuts keep the bus lengths exact); they differ in relaxation strength and model size.
backbone._bus_gateway_comment: 2026-11-03 (HANDOFF 16.26): true = every lane of a bus device (CAN / LIN / FlexRay) has one gateway unit on its line, which forwards the device data over the backbone to the units of its software (the zone-controller gateway); false = the units of the software sit on the line themselves. Default false; the gateway rule is an ablation row.
backbone._device_cable_factor_comment: 2026-11-03 (user decision): installed device connection = signal pair + power + ground cores; the factor multiplies the per-metre cost of every device-connected cable (direct device cables, Ethernet attachments, bus lines), not the backbone between units (no power). 3.0: an actuator's two 2.5 mm2 FLRY cores cost about as much again per metre as the signal pair (TME / Bedia reel prices), plus connectors and routing labour (low confidence). 1.0 = the signal-only model of the results before this date (ablation row).

_comment: cable_types: cost per metre, weight per metre, capacity = bit rate (Mbit/s, same units as flow volumes), port cost, hop_latency_ms = per-hop processing/queueing bound (switch forwarding, bus arbitration). Every type may connect two control units; the optimiser picks per data flow which type carries it. Latency of a message over a link of a type = message kbit / capacity + hop_latency_ms per hop (HANDOFF 14.3).
_data_comment: capacity = bit rate (Mbit/s), frame_kbit = longest frame of the type; data pass 2026-10-21, sources in data_source; hop_latency_ms, costs and weights unchanged (provisional, HANDOFF 17)
_cost_comment: All costs in USD (2026-10-22): cables per metre installed (wire price x harness factor), ports per end (transceiver or PHY plus half a connector pair), see cost_source; HANDOFF 17 F lists confidence.
_max_length_comment: 2026-11-03 (user decision, default): reach per cable type; no cable of a type may be longer: direct device cables keep the software within reach of the device, Ethernet attachments and backbone links out of reach do not exist, candidate paths use hops within reach, a bus line is at most this long. Replaces any ban of a type as backbone: SPI between two ECUs is possible only where they are within 1 m. Channel-graph distances as everywhere in the model.
